reason: Applanate means flattened.
Bearing glochids means glochids are present. FLOPO_0986043 is the glochid class in the anatomy registry.
Pencil-like means a slender cylinder.
Rectilinear means straight.
The verb form of anastomosing. Both are used for veins and other branches that join.
Oppositifolius means opposite a leaf, so leaf-opposed.
Pulpous means pulpy, which is fleshy.
Plane-convex is a spelling variant of plano-convex.
Radicant means rooting from the stem, which is shoot-borne roots present. The PO synonym list includes adventitious root.
Aerenchymatous means having aerenchyma.
Moundlike means a rounded mound, which is domed.
A falsely petiolate leaf has a narrowed base that looks like a petiole (a pseudopetiole). It does not mean the whole leaf tapers. Leave it unmapped or reject it.
Semispherical means hemispherical.
Gland is a synonym of this PO class, so without glands means glands absent.
Recumbent means lying on the ground. With the part constraint (plant, stem, branch) it is close to prostrate.
French soudés means fused, which is connate for parts of the same kind. It can mean adnate for parts of different kinds, but connate is the usual reading.
Panicked is a variant of panicled, meaning arranged in a panicle.
Voluminous means bulky, which is increased volume. It is vague, so confidence is moderate.
A misspelling of pedunculate.
Lanulose means finely woolly. Lanate is the nearest class, and only the diminutive sense is lost.
Vinelike means growing like a vine, which is climbing. It is in the same habit group as scandent.
The plain negation of beaked.
Uncolored means colorless.
Conchiform means shell-shaped.
Ramose means branched.
Broadly orbicular is still orbicular. Only the degree of breadth is lost, which a rule can accept.
Geocarpic means the fruit ripens underground, so it only applies to fruiting parts. Subterranean is the closest class for them.
The plain negation of adherent.
Eporose means without pores. Pores are not the same as perforations (perforate), so not perforate loses the meaning. Pore absence on the bearer is more exact.
Limbless fits leaf lamina absent only for leaf-like parts. For petals or a corolla, limb means something else.
Short-oval means a short ellipse, which is close to broadly elliptic. Only the ratio is lost.
French sacciforme means sac-shaped, which is saccate.
Trihedral means three-angled, which is trigonous in cross-section.
Diminished means reduced in size.
Even-sized means equal in size.
Limp means lacking stiffness, which is flexible. The plain reading fits.
A misspelling of pedicellate.
Villoso-ciliate means villous and ciliate. Mapping to ciliated alone loses the villous hairs. Split it into two qualities, or leave it unmapped.
The negation of foliaceous (leaf-like).
Coarsely serrate is still serrate. Only the degree is lost.
Blond means pale yellowish, and straw yellow is the nearest class. Confidence is moderate.
The PATO synonym needle-like is on subulate. Acicular would be the exact term, but subulate is close.
Thick-papery is the papery or chartaceous texture. Only the thickness is lost.
Closely arranged means approximate, in the sense of close together.
Interconnected means anastomosing only for veins and similar networks. For other parts it just means connected.
Lactiferous means bearing latex, which is laticifers present. The class is the cell that makes latex.
Rhombiform means rhomboid.
Narrowly cylindrical is still cylindrical. Only the degree is lost.
Eligulate means without a ligule.
The negation of nodose, which is knobbled.
